If you use a Nostr client, its settings have been readable by anyone who thought to ask the right relay.

NIP-78 defines kinds 78 and 30078, the events clients use to park per-user application data on a relay of the user's choosing. Settings, preferences, whatever an app decided to keep there. Until pull request 2458 merged on 3 September 2026, the specification said nothing at all about who was allowed to read them. Seven lines added, one removed.

It now says relays SHOULD run the NIP-42 AUTH flow before accepting or serving either kind, and SHOULD return them only to a client authenticated as the same pubkey that wrote them.

Two details are worth having right. The pull request is titled for kind 30078, but the text that merged covers kind 78 as well, so read the file and not the title. And the ownership check is against the event author, unlike NIP-17, which keys on the p tag because a gift wrap is signed by a throwaway key.

A SHOULD is a request, not a guarantee. The specification changing and your relay changing are two different events.

We read every NIP that merges and write up the ones that change what a relay owes the people using it. Which of your relays gate kind 30078 today, and do you know how you would check?
